name: p1-opentitan-uart-local-tlul-f1f5
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches the pinned OpenTitan UART TL-UL target in one process. F2/F4 exercise the register file, and F5 takes the device's real sticky tx_done interrupt: the firmware writes INTR_ENABLE/CTRL/WDATA, the UART really serializes the byte, intr_tx_done_o is delivered to the CPU input, the ISR reads INTR_STATE and clears it with the declared one-write W1C sequence.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one TL-UL target at 0x40003000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter; the UART profile's own MMIO endpoint is tl-ul/1 with address_width 32, data_width 32 and integrity required, so no APB3 target is in this build.
The target is opentitan_uart_local: the pinned uart.sv register block plus its local scalar wrapper, with the native serial pins as a scalar external_pins endpoint and nine native interrupt outputs.

The behavior file configs/behaviors/opentitan_uart_tx_done_f5.json is the declaration this scenario runs. It names intr_tx_done_o, the INTR_STATE word at 0, cause bit 2, the three trigger writes and a one-write clear_sequence that the executor performs as its single clear write.

rx=1 is the UART's idle serial level. The scenario holds it so the receiver can never observe a break or a frame error, and CTRL enables only the transmitter, so tx_done is the only event that can set an INTR_STATE bit during F5.
Window: the profile's own 4 KiB UART window at 0x40003000..0x40004000; it does not overlap the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and clears the 4 GiB bound.

No DMA is declared, so F6 is refused by name as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL. F1-F5 are runnable: the CPU exports RVFI retirement and a machine-external IRQ input, and the UART declares the four F5 facts plus a real W1C acknowledge.
This file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The run under runs/p1-replacements/ is the evidence, and it claims only what its case lines read from the device.
